standard-dialogue-before-throne-of-misce.npc: The King needs someone to take over the rule of the Kingdom. If I were you, I should consider the position.

standard-dialogue-before-royal-trouble.text: If the player recently killed a Miscellanian civilian:

steps.npc: Your Royal Highness, I should tell you right away that killing the people of this Kingdom will not make you popular with anyone.
Your subjects are worried about the possibility of war, but they are still happy to work for you.

options.text: Has anything been happening in the kingdom recently?
How do I manage the kingdom?
What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.player: What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.npc: Dealing with all the little troubles that come up from time to time, Your Royal Highness.
Such as the predicament we are now in.

steps.player: Has anything been happening in the kingdom recently?

steps.npc: Interesting that you should ask that, Your Royal Highness.
You see, the people are worried that war will break out again.
King Vargas has found himself with little to do now that you are the regent. He intended, at first, to return to adventuring.
Unfortunately, we still have not had the doors to the throne room enlarged so that he can leave...

steps.player: So, what has he been doing?

steps.npc: He has been trying to rule once more, in your absence. However, he has once again quarrelled with the Queen of Etceteria.
The two of them have been writing letters to each other, threatening to raise armies and declare war on each other once more!
Your Royal Highness, I suggest that you deal with this matter and reconcile the two of them again. Such a quarrel is not good for Miscellania.

steps.player: No, I don't have the time at the moment.

steps.npc: You are the regent of this kingdom, Your Royal Highness. I would urge you to reconsider.
However, you are also a busy hero, and thus I understand your reluctance.
Greetings, Your Royal Highness.

standard-dialogue-after-completing-royal.text: If the player is not engaged:

steps.npc: Greetings, Thane [Fremennik name].

steps.npc: Your Royal Highness, I should tell you right away that killing the people of this Kingdom will not make you popular with anyone.
Your subjects are content, your Highness.

steps.text: If the player is not engaged:

steps.npc: Your subjects are content, Thane [Fremennik name].

steps.text: If there is nothing to collect:

steps.npc: Your current approval rating is [number]%. I'm afraid your subjects have not yet collected anything.
Your current approval rating is [number]%. Would you like to collect the resources gathered by your subjects?

steps.text: If the player's bank is too full:

steps.npc: Let me check if you have made enough space in your bank, Your Royal Highness.
I'm afraid you will need [amount] more free space[s] in your bank to hold all the items your subjects have collected.

steps.text: If the player has enough space in their bank:

steps.npc: Here is a list of what your subjects have collected.
I shall tell your subjects to deliver your resources to your storage right away, Your Royal Highness.

steps.text: If the player is not engaged:

steps.npc: I shall tell your subjects to deliver your resources to your storage right away, Thane [Fremennik name].
This is how your subjects are distributing their effort.
Very well, Your Royal Highness.

steps.text: If the player is not engaged:

steps.npc: Very well, Thane [Fremennik name].
This is how your subjects are distributing their effort.

options.text: How do I manage the kingdom?

steps.player: How do I manage the kingdom?

steps.npc: Your loyal subjects work hard to collect resources for you. Every day they bring what they have collected to the castle. The resources which they collect are coal from the rocks to the north, maple logs from the trees

to the east, herbs from the garden just outside the castle, and tuna and swordfish fished at the port to the south. Etceteria has also pledged you teak and mahogany logs from their trees to the north, and seeds

from their farm to the south. They are paid from the money in the coffers; each day, one-tenth of the money in the coffers is distributed to them. A maximum of 75k is paid to your subjects and the Etceterians, and the

coffers can store up to 7.5 million gp. Another thing which affects the amounts of resources collected is your approval rating. The more your subjects love you, the more they will be motivated to work hard. King Vargas

would often go and help out his subjects in their daily tasks, when he was still able to do so, and they loved him dearly for it. Finally, you can choose how much of their efforts your subjects devote to each resource; of
course, the harder they work at collecting one, the less time they have to spend collecting the others.

steps.text: If the player does not have Ghrim's book:

steps.npc: Have you got a copy of my book? It explains everything in more detail.
Here, you can have this one, I have plenty spare.

steps.player: Thanks!{{^|Drops to ground with full inventory}}

options.text: What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.player: What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.npc: Ruling the Kingdom, Your Royal Highness.

steps.text: If the player is not engaged:

steps.npc: Ruling the Kingdom, Thane [Fremennik name].
And making sure that the king doesn't cause any more trouble.
